newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian parliament rejects budget cuts.
newsitem.headline: Russian parliament rejects budget cuts.

text.p: Russia's opposition-dominated lower house of parliament rejected by 210 votes to 112 on Monday a government bill to slash spending under the 1997 budget.

The State Duma also rejected by 195 to 137 votes a plan put forward by deputies themselves that would have cut spending by less than the 108 trillion roubles ($18.8 billion), or about one fifth of the budget, which the government was hoping for.

The government bill, which was receiving its first reading after weeks of stalling by the communist-led lower house, was prompted by a massive shortfall of more than 40 percent in tax revenue in the first three months of this year.

Reformist ministers had offered to reduce the amount of the cuts, known as sequestration, to about 88 trillion roubles ($15.3 billion) and to seek new sources of revenue. The opposition bill, put forward by a communist member, proposed cutting only 39 trillion roubles.

The government has said that, with or without the support of the Duma, which rises for the summer recess on Tuesday, cuts in spending will take place because the state is simply unable to pay its bills.

Deputy Finance Minister Vladimir Petrov told reporters after the vote that the government would hold talks with the Duma parties on Monday and Tuesday but would, in the absence of an accord, press on alone with bringing order to public finances.
